title: Rabbi Yehudah ben Gadish
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: [Eruvin 27a](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.27a.14) records his testimony before Rabbi Eliezer: “My father’s household used to buy fish-brine with second-tithe money.” Hyman gives the wording in [Tosefta Maaser Sheni, chapter 1](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosefta_Maaser_Sheni.1.14), as “My father’s household used to sell fish-brine in Jerusalem.” Hyman infers that he had seen the Temple while it still stood.

notes.text: Buying with second-tithe money and selling in Jerusalem are the two different formulations Hyman quotes. His conclusion that the witness had seen the standing Temple is an inference.

The Bavli reads Yehudah ben Gadish. The Tosefta’s Hebrew reads ben Gerush and brackets the words about selling brine in Jerusalem. Its accompanying English records Gadish as a variant. [Heilprin](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1634&lang=en) names Gadish and gives the wording about buying with tithe money.
